macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Global markets steadied as oil retreated after U.S.-Iran tensions rattled investors
items.summary: Reuters said U.S. stock index futures edged higher and European shares rose in choppy trading as markets reassessed the impact of fresh U.S. strikes on Iran and a rebound in technology stocks. Asian shares also climbed, but gains were capped by higher oil prices and renewed inflation concerns.

items.title: Oil prices rose on renewed Middle East conflict, stoking inflation worries
items.summary: Reuters reported that oil prices rose after fresh U.S. strikes on Iran dented hopes for an end to the conflict and for a full reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. TradingEconomics also noted that higher oil prices were weighing on bonds and reinforcing concern about energy-driven inflation.

items.title: Treasury yields stayed elevated as investors weighed inflation and geopolitical risks
items.summary: TradingEconomics said the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield was little changed at 4.58% after rising about 10 basis points over two sessions to a roughly two-month high. CNBC similarly reported that Treasury yields were steady as traders waited for domestic data amid the Iran flare-up.

items.title: ECB policymakers reportedly avoided forward guidance after June rate hike
items.summary: TradingEconomics reported that European Central Bank policymakers agreed not to provide guidance on the future path of rates, citing elevated uncertainty after June's first rate hike since 2023. The same feed said German Bund yields remained near multi-week highs as markets priced in more ECB tightening risk.

items.title: BOJ seen tightening as oil and inflation pressures persist
items.summary: Deloitte's weekly update said the Bank of Japan raised its benchmark rate by 25 basis points to 1%, the highest level since 1995. Reuters also noted that the 10-year Japanese government bond yield hit a 30-year high as oil prices revived inflation concerns.

items.title: S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures moved as tech stocks stabilized
items.summary: MarketScreener's live news stream said S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures ticked up as technology shares stabilized, while its 24-hour market list showed the S&P 500 down 1.44% and the Nasdaq 100 down 3.29%. Reuters also said European technology stocks helped lift regional shares.

items.title: Big stock swings highlighted risk-off tone in specific names
items.summary: MarketScreener's most-mentioned list showed sharp declines in Rheinmetall, Hyundai Motor, and Carnival, alongside a modest gain in Accenture. The same feed suggested investors were repricing cyclicals and defense-sensitive names amid the broader volatility.

items.title: IMF cut 2026 global growth forecast amid Iran war fallout
items.summary: Al Jazeera reported that the IMF trimmed its 2026 global growth outlook to 3% while citing fallout from the Iran war, even as AI demand helped offset some of the energy shock. The same report said trade and energy disruptions were central to the downgrade.

items.title: China producer inflation hit its fastest pace since 2022
items.summary: Reuters reported that China's producer price inflation accelerated for a fourth straight month in June to its highest level since July 2022, while consumer prices also rose. The data reinforced concerns that cost pressures remain elevated for manufacturers.

items.title: India inflation may have breached the central bank's 4% target
items.summary: Reuters said a poll showed India's consumer inflation likely exceeded the Reserve Bank of India's medium-term target in June for the first time in 16 months, driven by higher food and fuel prices. Reuters linked the pressure to the U.S.-Iran war, weak monsoon conditions, and elevated energy costs.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin falls as crypto stocks sell off; strategy and treasury plays tumble
items.summary: Bitcoin dropped sharply, and digital-asset treasury stocks including Strategy, BitMine, Sharplink, Solana Company, and Upexi sold off nearly 10% amid broader risk-off trading. CoinDesk also reported Bitcoin trading around $84K in this move.

items.title: European authorities seize $1.51B bitcoin-mixing service Cryptomixer
items.summary: Europol said it dismantled Cryptomixer, a crypto-mixing platform used by ransomware groups and darknet markets to launder bitcoin. Authorities seized servers, data, and about $29 million in BTC.

items.title: Canada moves toward stablecoin rules
items.summary: Canada is reportedly considering a stablecoin framework, with Scotiabank saying the proposal is aimed more at modernizing payments than broadly reshaping financial markets. The development adds to the growing regulatory focus on stablecoin oversight.

items.title: Bitcoin and major altcoins show mixed performance amid weekend selloff
items.summary: CoinDesk reported Bitcoin down 5.7% in its market update, with Bitcoin Cash also weaker. Other crypto prices in the broader market snapshot showed Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP, Solana, and Dogecoin trading with modest day gains on CryptoSlate, highlighting volatility across venues.

items.title: Polkadot breaks below $2.05 support level
items.summary: CoinDesk said DOT plunged 11% to around $2.02 on heavy volume, breaking a key support level and exposing the psychologically important $2.00 area. The move reflected pressure across altcoins during the wider selloff.

items.title: XRP, Bitcoin, and other majors recover in parts of the market
items.summary: Crypto and market trackers reported partial rebounds in major tokens, with Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP, Solana, Tron, Dogecoin, and Cardano posting gains in some snapshots. This suggests the market was volatile but not uniformly one-directional over the last 24 hours.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Work for workplace automation
items.summary: OpenAI unveiled ChatGPT Work, an agent designed to execute tasks across apps and files, intensifying competition in professional AI software. The launch follows a broader push by OpenAI into workplace productivity tools.

items.title: OpenAI releases GPT-Live voice models
items.summary: OpenAI launched GPT-Live, a new family of voice models that can listen and speak simultaneously in real time. The rollout targets more natural, low-latency voice interactions.

items.title: Meta opens developer access to Muse Spark 1.1
items.summary: Meta released developer access to Muse Spark 1.1, an upgraded AI model available through a public preview. Reuters said the release positions Meta more directly against OpenAI and Anthropic in paid model access for businesses.

items.title: xAI launches Grok 4.5 for coding and agentic tasks
items.summary: xAI introduced Grok 4.5, describing it as its most intelligent model yet and aiming it at coding and agentic workflows. The launch adds to the rapid pace of foundation model releases across the sector.

items.title: Anthropic adds Ben Bernanke to Long-Term Benefit Trust
items.summary: Anthropic appointed former U.S. Federal Reserve chair Ben Bernanke to its Long-Term Benefit Trust, an oversight body meant to keep the company aligned with its public mission. The move highlights growing attention to governance and safety structures at leading AI firms.

items.title: New York Times-led group seeks sanctions against OpenAI
items.summary: A group of newspapers led by The New York Times asked a federal court to sanction OpenAI in their copyright dispute, alleging the company misled the court about its ability to search systems for evidence related to training data. The case underscores continuing legal pressure on AI companies over content use.

items.title: Meta plans major Alberta data center for AI infrastructure
items.summary: Meta said it will build a large data center in central Alberta, its first in Canada, to expand compute capacity for AI. The announcement reflects the ongoing industry trend of heavy investment in infrastructure to support model training and deployment.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Sony says new PlayStation physical discs will end in January 2028
items.summary: Sony Interactive Entertainment clarified that production of physical game discs for new PlayStation titles will stop in January 2028, after which new games will be sold digitally through the PlayStation Store and at retail as digital codes. The move has sparked backlash and a consumer lawsuit, according to related reports.

items.title: Bethesda confirms Oblivion Remastered is coming to Switch 2
items.summary: Bethesda Softworks confirmed that The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered will launch on Nintendo Switch 2 on 11 August 2026. The announcement adds another notable third-party release to the new console's lineup.

items.title: Ubisoft announces The Crew Motorfest for Switch 2
items.summary: Ubisoft announced that The Crew Motorfest will launch on Nintendo Switch 2 on 8 October 2026. Physical retail editions will include a digital download code rather than a full game disc.

items.title: Epic Games settles lawsuit with former Fortnite leaker
items.summary: Epic Games reportedly reached a settlement with former contractor Hayden Cohen in its high-profile Fortnite leak case and dropped monetary claims. The dispute centered on allegations that confidential collaboration details had been leaked before official announcements.

items.title: Bungie reveals PvE mode Vault Breaker for Marathon
items.summary: Bungie unveiled Vault Breaker, a PvE mode for Marathon, with a launch date of 21 July and a notable gameplay twist. The reveal is one of the biggest recent updates for the shooter ahead of release.

items.title: Playstack releases Mortal Shell 2 trailer with release date
items.summary: Playstack published a new trailer for Mortal Shell 2 that officially revealed the game's release date and showed fresh gameplay footage. The update is a major announcement for fans of the soulslike series.

items.title: Guilty Gear: Strive surpasses 4 million players
items.summary: Arc System Works' Guilty Gear: Strive has passed 4 million players worldwide, setting a new franchise record. The game is also slated for release on 6 October 2026 for PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S.

items.title: Frostpunk 2 reaches 1 million copies sold
items.summary: 11 bit studios said Frostpunk 2 has sold 1 million copies across all platforms, marking a major commercial milestone. The company thanked fans while sharing the sales update.

items.title: Xbox reportedly increases investment in MachineGames
items.summary: Reports say Microsoft is significantly boosting investment in MachineGames following the commercial success of Indiana Jones and the Great Circle and the ongoing strength of the Wolfenstein franchise. The move suggests continued support for the studio's future projects.

items.title: EA shuts down Battlefield Hardline multiplayer servers
items.summary: Electronic Arts permanently closed the multiplayer servers for Battlefield Hardline on PlayStation and Xbox on 22 June 2026. Players on those platforms can now access only the single-player campaign.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: India scraps import duties on some electronics and smartphone parts
items.summary: India removed import duties on selected parts used to make mobile phones and other electronics, eliminating 7.5% and 5% levies. The move could benefit manufacturers including Apple and Xiaomi.

items.title: Apple to spend more than $30 billion under new Broadcom chip-supply deal
items.summary: Apple plans to spend more than $30 billion as part of a chip-supply agreement with Broadcom. The deal also includes Broadcom expanding a factory in Colorado.

items.title: Meta plans to start manufacturing an AI chip in September
items.summary: An internal memo reviewed by Reuters says Meta intends to begin manufacturing its own chip in September. The company is pursuing the chip to boost computing capacity next year.

items.title: EU lawmakers back temporary rules for detecting online child sexual abuse material
items.summary: EU lawmakers approved reinstating interim rules that would allow platforms such as Google and Meta to detect and remove child sexual abuse material. The proposal is intended to prevent a regulatory gap.

items.title: Coinbase restores prediction markets trading after technical issue
items.summary: Coinbase said it restored prediction markets trading after a technical problem disrupted the service. The incident was short-lived and the platform was brought back online.

items.title: Tesla settlement and Musk Twitter-share case approved by federal judge
items.summary: A federal judge approved the SEC’s settlement with Elon Musk over his purchase of Twitter shares. The ruling came despite the judge describing significant misgivings about the agreement.
